newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. team denied access to east Zaire by rebels.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team denied access to east Zaire by rebels.

text.p: U.N. investigators said they were leaving Rwanda on Saturday because rebels blocked their inquiry into reports of massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire.

A spokesman for the three-man investigative mission to east Zaire said it and a five-member team of forensic experts had waited in Rwanda since last Saturday for rebel clearance to start work in Zaire.

He said they were prepared to return once the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) gave assurances of "full and unconditional cooperation including security guarantees".

He said the team wanted to underline that it remained committed to fulfulling its mandate for a comprehensive, impartial and independent inquiry into numerous allegations of massacres and grave human rights violations in eastern Zaire.
He said two members of the investigative mission would fly back to Geneva from Rwanda and one would travel to New York.

The investigators and forensic experts had planned to dig up mass graves in a litmus test of rebel leader Laurent Kabila's willingness to assist human rights investigations. But the Tutsi-dominated rebels refused them access to rebel-held areas.

The blockage was an open challenge to the United Nations, whose top human rights body ordered the mission, and to western nations that condemned the alleged killings and urged Kabila to cooperate with the probe.
Washington said last week there were increasingly credible and shocking reports of killings of Hutu refugees in areas held by the rebels, who have seized about three-quarters of Zaire since October.
The U.N. mission on Friday accused the rebel alliance of trying to be "members of its own jury" by proposing to create its own team of national experts to work with the U.N. team.

It said the rebels also had serious reservations about the participation in the mission of U.N. human rights investigator for Zaire Roberto Garreton, who last month accused the rebels of continuing massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees and civilians.
The three-member U.N. commission was set up in April at the demand of Garreton, who said witness reports spoke of up to 50,000 Hutu refugees and civilians killed by the rebels.

The Hutus are the rump of two million Rwandans who fled to Zaire after Tutsi rebels ended the Hutu-led genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994 -- one of the worst mass slaughters of the 20th century.
